//// details | compose.yml: the agent, on every node, 38 lines, 3 notes
    type: example

each <span class="file-note-marker" title="note marker"></span> in the code opens a note on that line. [download compose.yml](../files/swarm/agent/compose.yml){ download="agent-compose.yml" }
{: .file-legend }

``` { .yaml .annotate linenums="1" }
services:
  agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.45.1
    environment:
      - TZ=America/Los_Angeles
      - AGENT_CLUSTER_ADDR=tasks.agent
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: /var/run/docker.sock
        target: /var/run/docker.sock
      - type: bind
        source: /var/lib/docker/volumes
        target: /var/lib/docker/volumes
      - type: bind  # (1)!
        source: /
        target: /host
        read_only: true
      - type: bind  # (2)!
        source: /usr/share/zoneinfo
        target: /usr/share/zoneinfo
        read_only: true
    ports:  # (3)!
      - target: 9001
        published: 9001
        protocol: tcp
        mode: host
    networks:
      - portainer
    deploy:
      mode: global
      placement:
        constraints:
          - node.platform.os == linux

networks:
  portainer:
    driver: overlay
    attachable: true
```

1.  the host's `/`, read-only. portainer only reads `/host` to show a node's devices and storage and to
    browse its files, and write access would add nothing but uploading, deleting and renaming files there.
2.  the agent image has no time zone data, so `TZ` alone changes nothing. the host's
    `/usr/share/zoneinfo` is mounted read-only.
3.  host mode, so the agent on the node that holds an address answers on it, the keepalived VIP
    included. through swarm's ingress, any node's agent could answer.
